scope: The 18 scored atoms on which the blind review of 3-4 November 2026 and the repository differ on whether the atom restates the pinned DCAT-AP base (relation_to_base = restates_base, restates_dcat_ap).
what_is_decided: For each of the 18 atoms, whether it restates the base, and its relation_to_base. 13 follow the blind review and 5 keep the repository's code. The other 178 scored atoms are not decided here: the review agrees with the repository on restates for all of them. For 31 of them it gives another code among tightens_base, extends_base, partly_base and beyond_base; these differences are not adjudicated and not applied.
method: Earlier coding. Until this record, the relation_to_base of the atoms of this record was the code given when the sets were built: the rows were split into atoms and coded in trace step R7 (22 October 2026 by the step's time order), and the independent check of the same date changed or confirmed some codes (next paragraph). The trace records who coded in R7 and the reasons as not recorded (gaps G-029 to G-032); relation_note is empty for every atom.

Earlier check, 22 October 2026. INDEPENDENT-CHECK.md records that a separate reviewer, who had not built the set, checked the draft atoms against the source texts and the DCAT-AP base files, among them all 45 atoms then coded as DCAT-AP restatements and all 111 term-level content atoms. Its table of findings names seven of the 18 atoms of this record: S-16.1, JRC-6.5, H-12.1, H-5.3, H-11.1 and H-11.2 (as H-11.x), and G-39.1 (for source flags only). Each item quotes the rows that name its atom in independent_check_2026_10_22.

Blind review, 3-4 November 2026. Eight Claude annotators (one per case; HealthDCAT-AP in three parts, mobilityDCAT-AP in two) coded the 196 scored atoms again. They saw the atom statements with their parts, the source's obligation wording and status, and the pinned base text. They did not see the repository's code, the extension profile or anything else in the repository. For each atom they answered restates or not first, then gave the seven-way code, the base class and property, the base obligation as read, a verbatim base quote and a rationale. According to the review's notes, every quoted base excerpt was checked by program to occur verbatim in the base text (whitespace-insensitive): 196 of 196, no failure.

Comparison, 4 November 2026. The review and the repository give the same code for 147 atoms and the same answer to restates for 178. Of the 49 differences, 11 change restates on the reading of the content, 7 change restates_base to tightens_base because the source asks more strongly than the base or adds a condition, and 31 leave restates as it is.

Decision sheet, 11 November 2026. The 18 atoms whose answer to restates differs were put before the curator with the statement, both codes, the base term, obligation and quote the review cited, and its rationale. The review fields were copied into the sheet and into this record by hand from the review table.

Curator's decisions, 11 November 2026, given in chat. First: all 18 follow the blind review except Req-18.1 and G-32.1, which keep the repository's code; the assistant that prepared the sheet had pointed to these two rows. Then, while this record was being made, the assistant found that several of the 18 atoms carry a note from the original curation that bears on the code; the blind reviewers had not seen the notes and the sheet had not shown them. Ten of the 18 atoms have a note. The assistant put five of them before the curator, in four questions: the curator kept the repository's code for S-16.1, followed the review for G-39.1 and JRC-6.5, and left H-11.1 and H-11.2 to the assistant, which kept the repository's code after reading the section of the reference document the notes point to. The other five notes were read by the assistant and not put before the curator: one agrees with the decision taken (Req-18.1), and in four the assistant found nothing against the review's reading (H-5.3, Req-19.2, Req-19.6, H-12.1). The field atom_note of each item says which.

After the decisions, while this record was being made, the assistant read INDEPENDENT-CHECK.md and found that the check of 22 October 2026 had settled the code of two atoms that now follow the blind review: H-5.3 (extends_base then, restates_base now) and H-12.1 (restates_base then, tightens_base now). The two findings were not before the curator at the decision. The pull request that carries this record asks the curator to confirm four rows before merging: these two, and H-11.1 and H-11.2, which the curator left to the assistant.

rule_in_force.B1_obligation: An atom whose source asks more strongly than the base (a requirement where the base recommends or allows) or adds a condition is tightens_base, not restates_base. The curator followed the review in six of the seven rows of this kind. In the seventh, S-16.1, the property stays recommended in the source according to the atom's note, so the source does not ask more strongly than the base, the rule does not apply and the atom keeps restates_base.
rule_in_force.geo_obligation_levels: Unchanged. The decision of 22 October 2026 (INDEPENDENT-CHECK.md, framing question) stands: INSPIRE and ISO obligation levels are kept as fields and are not part of each Geo need. No Geo atom changes on obligation grounds in this record; the three Geo atoms that change do so on the reading of the content.

limits: One blind AI review and the curator's adjudication of its differences from the earlier code on restates; two of the 18 rows were left to the assistant. No second human annotator took part. The findings of the independent check of 22 October 2026 were not shown to the blind reviewers and not in the decision sheet. The 31 differences that do not touch restates are not adjudicated. The review table (196 rows) is not in the repository. The base quotes of the mobilityDCAT-AP and HealthDCAT-AP atoms were not re-checked when this record was made, because the repository holds no copy of DCAT-AP 2.0.1 or 3.0.0. The blind reviewers did not see the notes field of the atoms; the notes of the 18 atoms were read when this record was made, those of the other 178 scored atoms were not compared with the review. Rows are not changed: the review read atoms, the scoring units.
